# Compiled Actuator Command Admission

This chapter records the F01/F09 development boundary for a versioned T01
`ACTUATOR_COMMAND` replay whose channel values are interpreted by the compiled
native actuator laws. The inventory provider and the executable physics
provider remain separate identities. In the current synthetic native fixture,
the inventory row is `myosuite/driver/default`, while the direct executor is
MuJoCo 3.8.0. That is development evidence for underlying MuJoCo replay; it
does not establish availability or qualification of the official MyoSuite
runtime.

## Profile and Execution Receipt

The T02 `compiled-actuator-profile/1.0.0` artifact is an opaque reference plus
SHA-256 digest at the structural interchange boundary. F09 resolves those
bytes, loads the registered direct model, and recomputes the canonical profile
from the loaded model and T01 replay bundle before stepping. The profile binds
the model source and loaded-model identities, execution provider and runtime,
native actuator laws and ordered channels, complete initial-state digest,
applied-input digest, time grid, replay policy, and verified resource closure.
A matching T02 string or digest alone is not native execution evidence.

F09 returns a frozen `NativeActuatorCommandReceipt` linked to the native output
digest. The receipt carries the separate inventory-to-execution correspondence
and the horizon of the submitted T01 bundle; it does not establish the duration
or completeness of an original capture. F01 contract `feedback-comparison/1.2.0` admits that receipt for
within-engine replay only when its identities and payload digests match the
comparison evidence. The receipt is an integrity record, not a signature or a
cryptographic attestation: deserialized caller-supplied receipts remain claims
until a verifier independently checks their lineage or repeats the native
execution. The API does not certify physics or physiology.

## Mixed Compiled Laws Are Not Muscle-Only Drive

`ACTUATOR_COMMAND` preserves each native channel's compiled transmission,
dynamics, gain/bias/force law, target and order. A model may combine motors,
muscles, filters, or other native actuator types. Therefore the coarse
inventory drive label cannot establish that a run was fully muscle-driven;
even zero motor commands do not prove muscle-only assistance. F01 explicitly
rejects that claim for the compiled-command pathway. A separately reviewed
assistance policy and corresponding native evidence are required.

Within-engine replay may compare identical source and loaded model, execution
provider, compiled profile, full initial state, policy, input history, channel
order, and horizon. Cross-engine `SAME_INPUT` does not equate dimensionless
command values or compiled profiles. It requires a separately reviewed
semantic mapping. Required inventory rows remain in the denominator when a
runtime or model binding is unavailable.

## Evidence Limits

Synthetic tests use a direct MuJoCo fixture and independently rehashed profile
mutations. They exercise exact binding and negative admission cases, not a
production MyoSuite package, full-body model, human capture, or a numerical
acceptance tolerance. The six-engine parity and muscle-driven OpenSim goals
remain open.

F09 runtime consumers obtain Tools T01 types through the single
`native_replay_contract_types()` facade. Its pinned package loader uses a
private module name and does not extend `sidekick.lab.__path__`; this keeps
execution, observation admission and tests on one canonical class/enum
identity without publishing a second `sidekick.lab.mocap` module.
